episodes.160760: Morning storms produce strong marine wind gust in Sarasota waters west of Siesta Key.
episodes.160766: The remnants of Hurricane Ida produced widespread heavy rainfall across Pennsylvania. Additionally, thunderstorms were observed southeast Of I-81 and the PA Turnpike. One of these storms produced wind damage in Adams County.
episodes.160871: A front dropped south into the ArkLaMiss region. Ahead of this front, warming occurred which combined with ample moisture to produce thunderstorms. Some storms were severe with damaging winds being the primary concern.
episodes.161032: A line of thunderstorms stretching from the Volusia County nearshore waters southwest across northern Brevard and eastern Orange counties, moved east and offshore. One embedded cell briefly produced severe wind gusts, which were measured at the Shuttle Landing Facility (KTTS).
episodes.161036: A line of thunderstorms stretching from the nearshore Volusia county waters back into north Brevard and eastern Orange counties, produced strong to severe wind gusts across |northern Brevard county near the Merritt Island National Wildlife Refuge as it quickly pushed east and offshore.
episodes.161500: A weak surface trough backdoored southwest into North Central Louisiana during the late afternoon and evening hours of September 1st, which was reinforced by a weakness aloft over the Lower Mississippi Valley rounding the upper ridge anchored over the Central and Southern Plains. Compressional warming ahead of this surface trough resulted in temperatures climbing into the upper 90s to near 100 degrees across North Central Louisiana, contributing to moderate to strong instability over this area. This instability, and the weakness aloft, resulted in strong vertical forcing such that scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed just ahead of the surface trough across Southwest Arkansas and North Central Louisiana, producing damaging winds which downed trees across portions of Union and Ouachita Parishes before weakening during the evening with the gradual loss of instability.
episodes.161911: Severe thunderstorm on the 1st produced severe hail near Bridgeport and wind gusts of 66 MPH near Alliance. Received numerous reports of cars with cracked windshields due to hail along US Highway 26 between Bridgeport and Scottsbluff.
episodes.162028: A front dropped south into the ArkLaMiss region. Ahead of this front, warming occurred which combined with ample moisture to produce thunderstorms. Some storms were severe with damaging winds being the primary concern.
episodes.162287: The remnants of Ida trigger Severe Thunderstorms across Southeastern New York.
episodes.162289: The remnants of Ida trigger severe thunderstorms across Southern Connecticut.
episodes.162292: The remnants of Ida trigger severe thunderstorms across Northeastern New Jersey.
episodes.162293: The remnants of Ida trigger severe thunderstorms across the coastal waters.
episodes.162386: An isolated severe storm moved across central Kansas on September 2nd, 2021.  The storm produced a a severe wind gust to 70 mph in Ellsworth county, Kansas. Also widespread rainfall amounts of 2 to 4 inches occurred across much of the area, with the highest rainfall total occurring in Russell county with 3.65 inches.
episodes.162538: Post Tropical Cyclone Ida brought heavy rain to New Jersey on September 1.  Rainfall totals were as high as 5 to 10 inches.  The heavy rain caused significant flash flooding, mainly in the northern half of the state.  It resulted in widespread property damage.  There were several fatalities.
episodes.162543: Thunderstorms developed during the morning hours affiliated with a passing cold front and approaching upper level short-wave trough. A few of these storms became severe, producing one-inch diameter hail over Mountrail and Slope counties. Over Renville County, 60 mph wind gusts were reported.
episodes.162660: An isolated summer thunderstorm resulted in a 50 knot wind gust at KABY airport. In addition, a brief funnel cloud was reported near Nashville.
episodes.162823: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a warm front situated across the western Nebraska Panhandle during the late evening hours of September 1st. As activity transitioned east, it became severe with strong damaging wind gusts. Estimated wind gusts up to 70 MPH were reported south of Merriman.
episodes.162971: The remnants of Tropical Cyclone Ida resulted in widespread flash flooding over Ulster and Dutchess Counties during the late evening of September 1 where 3 to 7 inches of rain fell. The southern half of Dutchess County was hit hardest, where 35 roads were damaged or closed and at least one bridge washed out. The County Executive declared a state of emergency and restricted non-essential travel for several towns in southern Dutchess. Metro North rail service was shut down due to the flooding, and up to 2,000 customers lost power. A federal major disaster was declared for Dutchess County, which reported $2.5 million in damages to public assets and municipal facilities, along with an estimated $1 million in damages to private homes, apartments, and businesses.
episodes.162973: The remnants of Tropical Cyclone Ida resulted in several reports of flash flooding over during the early morning hours of September 2. Rainfall from the evening of the 1st through the early morning hours of the 2nd totaled three to six inches. Several roads were closed as a result of the flooding, and one fatality occurred when a police officer's patrol vehicle was swept away by flood waters.
episodes.162998: The combination of high pressure sinking southward and Tropical Depression Ida over the  Northeast U.S. allowed for a mid-level trough and deep moisture to sink southward across the region. This prompted light S to SW flow, which pushed the Gulf Sea Breeze inland and towards the east coast while the Atlantic Sea Breeze pinned along the east coast. A few strong thunderstorms developed across the area as a result.
episodes.162999: The combination of high pressure sinking southward and Tropical Depression Ida moving across the NE United States allowed for a mid-level trough and deep moisture to sink southward across the region. This prompted light S to SW flow, which pushed the Gulf Sea Breeze inland and towards the east coast while the Atlantic Sea Breeze pinned along the east coast. With adequate moisture and shear, strong storms developed, especially in areas where the sea breezes collided. Heavy rain and flooding were the main hazards.
episodes.163000: The combination of high pressure sinking southward and Tropical Depression Ida over the Northeast U.S. allowed for a mid-level trough and deep moisture to sink southward across the region. This prompted light S to SW flow, which pushed the Gulf Sea Breeze inland and towards the east coast while the Atlantic Sea Breeze pinned along the east coast. With adequate moisture and shear, strong storms developed, especially in areas where the sea breezes collided. Multiple waterspouts and strong winds were reported across the Gulf waters.
episodes.163048: On Sept. 1, Tropical Depression Ida tracked northeasward from the central Appalachians and arrived in southern New England late in the day as a remnant low. The low moved rather swiftly across southern New England, reaching the coastal waters east of Massachusetts by 7 AM EDT on Sept. 2.  Heavy rain of 4.5 to 6.5 inches fell in northern Connecticut, with the most intense rain falling from the evening on the 1st to the early morning on the 2nd. There was widespread flash flooding.  As a result of the heavy rainfall and extensive flooding, Governor Lamont issued a State of Emergency for the state of Connecticut.
episodes.163049: On Sept. 1, Tropical Depression Ida tracked northeasward from the central Appalachians and arrived in southern New England late in the day as a remnant low. The low moved rather swiftly across southern New England, reaching the coastal waters east of Massachusetts by 7 AM EDT on Sept. 2.  Heavy rain of 4.0 to more than 8.0 inches fell across Rhode Island, with the most intense rain falling from the evening on the 1st to the early morning on the 2nd.  In Portsmouth, a CoCoRAHS observer recorded 8.32 inches of rain for the event.  There was widespread street flooding and some flash flooding in Rhode Island.
episodes.163050: On Sept. 1, Tropical Depression Ida tracked northeasward from the central Appalachians and arrived in southern New England late in the day as a remnant low. The low moved rather swiftly across southern New England, reaching the coastal waters east of Massachusetts by 7 AM EDT on Sept. 2.  One to three inches of rain fell in northwest Massachusetts, but heavy amounts of 4.0 to 6.5 inches fell south of the Mass Pike, with the heaviest amounts, near 7 inches, in the upper portion of Cape Cod.  The most intense rain fell from the evening on the 1st to the early morning on the 2nd. There was widespread street flooding and some flash flooding.  In addition, a brief tornado touched down in Dennis, MA (on Cape Cod) during the overnight hours.
episodes.163088: A few late afternoon showers formed in the moisture left over from the remnants of tropical system Nora. While no lightning was detected, a funnel cloud was observed near Sonoita.
episodes.163121: A surge of tropical moisture, combined with a an upper level low centered over an area near state borders of Arizona, Nevada and California is producing moderate rainfall over|central and northern Arizona.
episodes.163134: Lingering monsoon moisture fueled a few thunderstorms in Mohave County. One storm produced flash flooding.
episodes.163158: Isolated thunderstorms developed during the afternoon of the 2nd across northwest Oklahoma, with an isolated severe wind gust reported.
episodes.163204: The remnants of Ida produced widespread flooding along with instances of flash flooding across the area. Tropical moisture infiltrated the area and there were moderate amounts of instability as well. This combined with the lift provided from the remnants of Ida led to heavy rainfall during this time. Rainfall amounts averaged around 1-3 near and east of Interstate 95, with amounts around 4 to 8 inches across portions of northern and central Maryland. Excess runoff from the heavy rainfall led to river flooding as well.
episodes.163217: On the evening of September 1st, a lee surface trough moved into the east-central Colorado region which caused thunderstorms to develop in the area. As a result, an intense microburst formed near the Burlington Colorado airport. The strong winds associated with this microburst then spread to the north, impacting the eastern portions of the community of Burlington. This storm produced a swath of damage in excess of 4 miles long, with the most intense damage occurring between the airport and Interstate 70. The damaging winds from the microburst were estimated to be up to the 100-115 mph range.
episodes.163224: On September 1st, a lee surface trough moved near the Colorado/Kansas border which allowed evening thunderstorms to develop in northwestern Kansas. These thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts up to 70 mph.
episodes.163232: A shield of moderate to heavy rainfall, associated with the remnants of tropical cyclone Ida, moved from the DelMarVa peninsula to New England. This rainfall on top of several weeks of abnormally wet weather led to areas of small stream and urban flash flooding in Central New York.
episodes.163233: A shield of moderate to heavy rainfall, associated with the remnants of tropical cyclone Ida, moved from the DelMarVa peninsula to New England. This rainfall on top of several weeks of abnormally wet weather led to areas of small stream and urban flash flooding in Northeast Pennsylvania.
episodes.163260: Extremely heavy rainfall associated with the remnants of Hurricane Ida overspread southern Connecticut during the evening of September 1 and continued through the early morning hours of September 2. Rainfall totals ranged from 5-8+ inches across much of the region, with much of that rain falling in just a few hours. This resulted in not only widespread flash flooding but also extensive river flooding. The ASOS at Bridgeport Airport recorded 5.59 inches of rain. A CoCoRaHS observer near Stamford recorded 8.10 inches of rain, while another in Uncasville reported 8.58 inches. Broadcast media reported 8.37 and 8.90 inches in Clinton and near Madison, respectively.
episodes.163286: Two rounds of storms occurred late on 9/2 and early on 9/3, producing isolated wind damage and flash flooding.
episodes.163420: Several rounds of thunderstorms brought severe weather hazards to the state of Utah, including flash flooding in southern and eastern Utah, and damaging winds, hail, and a tornado in Northern Utah.
episodes.163444: Weak southwest flow aloft brought up the remnants of Hurricane Nora into the Borderland. Heavy rain fell across Far West Texas with flash flooding reported in El Paso and Hudspeth counties.
episodes.163518: Extremely heavy rainfall associated with the remnants of Hurricane Ida overspread northeast New Jersey during the evening of September 1 and continued through the early morning hours of September 2. Rainfall totals ranged from 5-8+ inches across much of the region, with much of that rain falling in just a few hours. The ASOS at Newark Airport recorded 8.44 inches of rain, while the ASOS at Teterboro Airport recorded 7.14 inches. A COOP observer in Harrison recorded 8.72 inches of rain. This resulted in widespread flash flooding leading to numerous road closures and water rescues in addition to extensive river flooding. Eight people died as a result of the flash flooding and one person remains missing.
episodes.163547: An outflow boundary from convection over the southern mainland of Florida interacted with island-heating-induced cloud lines over the Florida Keys in an area of weak ridging. Scattered showers and thunderstorm developed as the two features interacted, resulting in isolated gale-force wind gusts offshore the far upper Florida Keys.
episodes.163555: Extremely heavy rainfall associated with the remnants of Hurricane Ida overspread southeast New York during the evening of September 1 and continued through the early morning hours of September 2. Rainfall totals ranged from 5-8 inches across much of the region, with much of that rain falling in just a few hours. The ASOS at Central Park recorded 7.19 inches of rain, including 3.15 inches in a single hour between approximately 9:00-10:00pm. This resulted in widespread catastrophic flash flooding across New York City that resulted in extensive road and subway closures and numerous water rescues. Additional rainfall totals from around the region include 7.38 inches at a New York Mesonet station in Fordham in the Bronx, a report of 7.00 inches from a CoCoRaHS observer in Boerum Hill, Brooklyn, 6.90 inches from the ASOS at LaGuardia Airport, a spotter report of 6.18 inches in Monroe, a spotter report of 8.09 inches in Scarsdale, and a CoCoRaHS report of 6.72 inches in Locust Valley. Ultimately 17 people died as a result of the flash flooding, including 13 in New York City and 4 in the Lower Hudson Valley.

events.narrative: Widespread flash flooding occurred in Sussex County with numerous road closures.

The Peckman River at Ozone Avenue in Verona rose above its minor flood stage of 3.5 feet at 8:00pm EDT. It then continued to rise, surpassing moderate flood stage (4.0 feet) at 8:10pm EDT, then major flood stage (5.0 feet) at 8:25pm EDT before cresting at a height of 6.20 feet at 9:20pm EDT. The river then slowly fell over the next few hours, returning to its banks at 12:40am EDT on September 2nd.
Flash flooding resulted in an estimated $10 million in damages across Orange County, which includes $1 million in individual damages and $9 million in public assistance.
Trees were blown down and blocked the roadway on Jackson Raymond Road near Springridge Road. One tree fell onto a house on Springridge Road.
Elaine Place in Monsey was closed due to flooding.
The Conestoga River at Lancaster crested at 18.49 feet at 930 am EDT on 9/2, which is in major flood stage.
The Bronx River Parkway was closed southbound in White Plains due to flooding.
A brief funnel cloud was reported near Nashville.
A water rescue was ongoing at the intersection of White Oak Ridge Road and Mohawk Road in Millburn with a vehicle stranded in flood waters.

The Third River at Bloomfield rose above its minor flood stage of 6.0 feet at 8:10pm EDT. The river then continued to rise, surpassing moderate flood stage (8.0 feet) at 8:45pm EDT and major flood stage (9.0 feet) at 9:05pm EDT before cresting at a height of 10.14 feet at 11:30pm EDT. After cresting, the river quickly fell back below minor flood stage by 3:45am EDT September 2nd. The crest of 10.14 feet is the highest on record for this location, exceeding the previous record crest of 9.97 feet in September 1999 due to Hurricane Floyd.
All southbound lanes of NJ Route 17 were closed due to flooding north of Century Road in Paramus.
All were closed on US Routes 1&9 at East Grand Street in Elizabeth due to flooding.
ASOS station KAIA - Alliance Airport 5 miles southeast of Alliance reported wind gust.
A short-lived funnel cloud was reported and captured on video near Sonoita.

The water level rose into major flood stage, cresting at 22.10 feet at 2:15 PM on the 2nd of September. ||The water level rose above flood stage, cresting at 19.03 feet at 4:45 AM on the 23rd of September. Significant lowland flooding occurred along the river, with backwater flooding also occurring. Numerous roads were closed. Water reached the parking lot at Gambrill Mill along the Monocacy Battlefield. Backwater flooding from Carroll Creek also approached the underside of the bridge leading to the Frederick city wastewater treatment plant. ||Maryland Route 26 was flooded near the Monocacy River bridge and water reached Gambrill Mill on the Monocacy National Battlefield. Much of Pinecliff Park and Rivermist Park were flooded. Buckeystown Community Park was also flooded.
Ashburton Avenue in Yonkers was closed near the Saw Mill River Parkway due to flooding.
A tree fell onto a house in the Rocky Branch community.
Multiple rescues were needed across Livingston for occupied cars stranded in flood waters.

Seven people were injured when the roof of the U.S. Postal Service's bulk mail facility on Harrison Avenue in Kearny collapsed due to heavy rain. 300 people were inside at the time. There were also multiple roads in the area with significant flooding.

The Rahway River near Springfield rose above its minor flood stage of 7.0 feet at 8:30pm EDT. It then continued to rise, surpassing moderate flood stage (8.5 feet) at 9:15pm EDT and major flood stage (10.5 feet) at 11:45pm EDT before cresting at a height of 10.81 feet at 1:15am EDT on September 2nd. The crest of 10.81 feet is the second highest on record, behind only a crest of 10.88 feet in August 2011 associated with Tropical Storm Irene. The river then gradually fell through the overnight hours, eventually fallign back below minor flood stage at 12:45pm EDT on September 2nd.
Mountain Lodge Road in Washingtonville was closed due to flooding.
A roof was damaged at Ford Plaza in West Monroe. Trees and power lines were downed, and a fence was toppled near Kiroli Park from Good Hope Road to Arkansas and Wallace Roads.
Report received via mPing of a thunderstorm wind gust that blew shingles off of a structure and broke off 1-inch tree limbs near this location. Wind speed is estimated based on damage indicators.
Flash flooding resulted in an estimated $60 million in damages across Staten Island, and an estimated $300 million city-wide. This estimate only includes FEMA and SBA fund requests.
KSYF AWOS recorded a 69 mph thunderstorm wind gust at location.

Flash flooding resulted in an estimated $3,126,485 in damages across Rockland County. This estimate is based on FEMA grant money awarded under the Individuals and Household Program (IHP), which includes funds for both housing assistance and other needs.
The Fire Department was responding to a report of basement flooding endangering and electrical panel on Hamilton Avenue in Glen Rock.
Multiple roads were closed due to flooding in town of Kearny including Passaic Avenue, Harrison Avenue near the Walmart, and Route 7.
Flash flooding led to a road collapse of South Main Street near Earth Conservancy Drive.

A significant flash flood occurred in the town of Hanksville, with nearly every structure in town impacted by flooding. Floodwaters were reportedly as deep as 6 feet in places. Rainfall totals were 1.2 inches in Hanksville, and were as high as 1.7 inches in the Henry Mountains. In Capitol Reef National Park, 1.66 inches fell.
EMS reported multiple water rescues ongoing across Union County due to significant flash flooding. A few evacuations were occurring as well.

The Saddle River at Upper Saddle River rose above its minor flood stage of 4.5 feet at 9:00pm EDT. It then continued to rise, reaching moderate flood stage (5.0 feet) at 9:15pm EDT before cresting at a height of 5.43 feet at 10:45pm EDT. This crest was the second highest on record, falling just short of the record crest of 5.64 feet in September 1999 associated with Hurricane Floyd. The river then fell back below minor flood stage at 1:45am EDT on September 2nd.
Water was flooding into the basements of many homes in the Todt Hill section of Staten Island and sewer mains were overflowing.
Numerous water rescues were ongoing in Livingston. Rescue boats were pulling occupants to safety on Walnut Street, East Hobart Gap Road, and Old Short Hills Road.
A thunderstorm wind gust of 59 mph was measured at the Teterboro ASOS.
Tree down into house with structural damage on Voorhees Road.
Cars were stuck in flood waters at the intersection of Crystal Avenue and College Avenue in Westerleigh.
Barbour Street in Haledon was closed due to flooding.

The Pascack River at Park Ridge rose above its minor flood stage of 5.2 feet at 9:15pm EDT. It then continued to rise, surpassing moderate flood stage (6.2 feet) at 9:45pm EDT and major flood stage (7.2 feet) at 11:30pm EDT. The river then crested at a height of 7.44 feet at 12:15am EDT September 2nd. The river then gradually receded overnight, falling back below minor flood stage at 4:30am EDT September 2nd.

Multiple water rescues were occurring on Route 208 at Russell Avenue in Wycoff.

Several roads were closed in the town of Fishkill and city of Beacon due to flash flooding. The County Executive declared a state of emergency and restricted all non-essential travel due to the flooding.

Several roads were closed in the town of Beekman due to flash flooding. The County Executive declared a state of emergency and restricted all non-essential travel due to the flooding.
Several roads were closed in the town of Pawling due to flash flooding. The County Executive declared a state of emergency and restricted all non-essential travel due to the flooding.
Local roads were closed in Westwood due to flooding. Houses were flooding with water entering basements.

The Saddle River at Lodi rose above its minor flood stage of 6.0 feet at 9:30pm EDT. It then continued to rise, surpassing moderate flood stage (7.0 feet) at 10:00pm EDT and major flood stage (8.0 feet) at 11:00pm EDT before cresting at a height of 12.57 feet at 9:00am EDT on September 2nd. The river then gradually receded, eventually falling below minor flood stage at 8:00pm EDT on September 2nd. The crest of 12.57 feet is the fourth highest on record at this location.

The Saddle River at Ridgewood rose above its minor flood stage of 5.0 feet at 9:30pm EDT. The river then continued to rise, surpassing moderate flood stage (6.0 feet) at 10:00pm EDT and major flood stage (7.0 feet) at 10:45pm EDT before cresting at a height of 12.01 feet at 12:45am EDT on September 2nd. The river then gradually fell overnight, eventually receding below minor flood stage again at 6:15am EDT September 2nd.
Widespread road closure along the Bronx River Parkway in Greenville due to flooding.

A 55 year old man was found dead on Ridgewood Road in the vicinity of Berkeley Road in Maplewood due to flooding. He is believed to have been swept away by flood waters while attempting to remove debris from drains in the area.

A 66 year old man and his 46 year old daughter died as a result of flooding after going into the basement of their home on Lincoln Place in Irvington to secure it as the Elizabeth River began to overflow.

A car carrying two Seton Hall University students was overcome by flood waters on Main Avenue near Benson Avenue in Passaic. The body of one of the students, a 21 year old man, was later found in Newark after being swept down the Passaic River.

A car carrying two Seton Hall University students was overcome by flood waters on Main Avenue near Benson Avenue in Passaic. The body of one of the students, an 18 year old woman, was later found in Kearny after being swept down the Passaic River.
An unidentified person died by electrocution as a result of flooding in Essex County.
One person died at a hospital in Bergen County after pushing their car through flood waters and suffering a medical event.
Water rescues were ongoing for several occupied stranded cars on Route 17 near Racetrack Road in Ho-Ho-Kus.
Significant flooding was occurring on the ground level of Terminal B at Newark Airport. Flooding was occurring on the baggage level as well.
Numerous cars were underwater on the West Shore Expressway with occupants standing on roofs of cars waiting to be rescued.
Several trees were blown down in Byram. Trees blocked the roadway at Springridge Road and Owens Road. Trees also blocked the roadway on Siwell Road at Byram Estates.
Basement and garage flooding were reported in Livingston.
Significant flooding was reported on 20th Avenue in Paterson with several cars submerged.
Flooding was occurring over Route 52A near the Stone Arch Bridge historical site.
Severe flooding was occurring on the Palisades Parkway between North Middletown Road (Exit 10) and New Hempstead Road (Exit 11) in New City.
NJ Route 36 was closed at Main Street in Port Monmouth due to flooding.
NJ Business Route 33 was closed between Wemrock Road and Cardigan Bay Lane in Freehold Township due to flooding.
The southbound Saw Mill River Parkway was flooded at Clarence Avenue in Hastings-on-Hudson.

It then continued to rise, surpassing moderate flood stage (6.0 feet) by 1:00am EDT September 2nd and major flood stage (6.5 feet) at 3:15am EDT. The river crested at a height of 7.42 feet at 5:15am EDT September 2nd. The river receded throughout the morning, falling back below flood stage at 11:15am EDT September 2nd.

NJ Route 73 in Palmyra was closed due to flooding.
US Route 30 was closed near the Airport Circle in Pennsauken Township due to flooding.
Prospect Avenue, Old Hook Road, and Broadway were all closed due to flooding and cars with occupants trapped.

The bridge at Westmore Gardens in Englewood was knocked off its foundation due to rising waters from Overpeck Creek. Two cars then crashed into the bridge.

The Ramapo River near Mahwah rose above its minor flood stage of 8.0 feet at 10:00pm EDT. It then continued to rise, climbing above moderate flood stage (9.0 feet) at 11:15pm before cresting at a height of 10.46 feet at 3:00am EDT on September 2nd. The river then slowly fell over the next day, with water levels eventually falling below minor flood stage at 10:45am EDT on September 3rd. This was the 11th highest crest on record at this location.

Four people died due to flooding at the Oakwood Plaza apartment complex on Irvington Avenue in Elizabeth. All four people were found in one apartment and included a 74 year old woman, her 71 year old husband, their 38 year old son, and a 33 year old neighbor.
An 83 year old man was found on Chestnut Street in Union Township near Overlook Hospital. He is believed to have drowned after his car got stuck and he walked out into 3-4 feet of water.
East Sunnyside Lane was flooded and impassable in Irvington with water more than a foot deep in spots. Widespread flooding was also occurring elsewhere in the village.
A 50 year old man, 48 year old woman, and 2 year old boy died when a basement apartment on 64th Street near Laurel Hill Boulevard in Elmhurst, Queens flooded.
Homes and basements were flooding on Woodbine Street in Ridgewood, Queens.
A basement was flooded in Howard Beach, Queens.
Queens Boulevard in Maspeth and Corona has about 2-4 feet of flowing water running across the street. Multiple cars were stranded.
A large tree down on New Street took down some wires.
One to two feet of water was covering the road with cars disabled in the roadway on 2nd Avenue between 59th Street and 60th Street in Bay Ridge, Brooklyn.

Intense straight line winds due to the microburst first occurred at 8:12 PM MDT near the Burlington airport. This began an area of intermittent damage consistent with wind speeds in the 100-115 mph range. The most intense winds occurred over an area 4.2 miles long and 600 yards wide, ending near Interstate 70 and the Kit Carson Correctional facility. The most significant damage occurred near the Burlington airport where a large evergreen tree was snapped at the trunk and near the Kit Carson Correctional Facility where four power poles were snapped and a nearby outbuilding was destroyed. Damage due to winds in the 60-80 mph range continued to the north of Interstate 70. Additional storm damage included: uprooted trees; damage to the wind and visibility sensors of the KITR ASOS, a camper trailer, overhead garage doors (blown in/dented), fences, windows, siding and roofs of outbuildings and a mobile home; and the flipping of shipping containers and semi-truck trailers. The city of Burlington also lost power as a result of the storm damage.
A car was stuck in 2.5 feet of water at the intersection of Berdan Avenue and Sunnyside Drive in Fair Lawn. Additional flooding was reported on multiple roads across the town.
Several cars drove around barricades in Rye and are now stuck in flood waters.
The Fremont River overflowed its banks between Hanksville and Caineville, making state Route 24 impassible east of Capitol Reef National Park.
Wires down across Natoma Street and Purchase Street.
Several water rescues took place in Keyport.

The Passaic River at Dundee Dam in Clifton rose above its minor flood stage of 4.5 feet at 10:15pm EDT and crested at a height of 4.98 feet at 12:45am EDT September 2nd. The river then fell back below flood stage at 3:45am EDT on September 2nd. Flooding from the Passaic River resulted in three fatalities. A 70 year old man died when his car became stranded in 6 feet of water at the intersection of Passaic Avenue and Lackawana Place in Passaic.

The Bronx River at the New York Botanical Garden rose above its minor flood stage of 3.0 feet at 10:15pm EDT. It then continued to quickly rise, surpassing moderate flood stage (3.5 feet) at 10:45pm EDT and major flood stage (4.0 feet) at 11:30pm EDT. The river ultimately crested at a height of 5.59 feet at 8:45am EDT on September 2nd. It eventually fell back below minor flood stage at 9:30pm EDT on September 2nd.

Tree down across Playland Parkway between Forest Avenue and Midland Avenue.

Route 9W was reported closed at Perkinsville Road due to flooding.
Route 209 at Old Minisink Trail was reported closed due to flooding.
Briggs Highway was reported closed due to flooding.
Berme Road was reported closed due to flooding.
Water was reported over the bridge on Gardner Hollow Road near Buck Drive. The road was reported impassable.
Noxon Road and Colonial Drive was reported flooded and impassable.
Only one lane on Titusville Road, Phillips Road, and Old Manchester Road was reported open due to flooding.
Ten Mile River Drive at Stephens Road was reportedly closed due to flooding.
County Road 23 Chestnut Ridge at Killean Road in Union Vale was reported closed due to flooding.
County Route 111 was reported closed due to flooding.
County Road 24 north of Camby Road in Dover reportedly had water running over the road making it impassable.
Flooding was reported in a basement in Parkchester in the Bronx with water three feet deep.
Water was spilling into a home in Crown Heights through the doors as the ground drains became either overwhelmed or clogged. Two inches of water was in the basement.
Two women and a man died when their basement apartment flooded on Peck Avenue near Kissena Boulevard in Flushing, Queens.
A 33 year old man from the Bronx died when he drove his vehicle into flood waters on South Columbus Avenue in Mount Vernon and became trapped.
The body of a 69 year old man was found near Route 119 near the Mario Cuomo Bridge in Tarrytown not far from where his car was found submerged.

An elderly couple's vehicle was found pinned against a utility pole at the intersection of Lincoln Avenue and Brookside Way in Rye Brook. The couple are believed to have been swept away from their vehicle and down Blind Brook Creek and drowned.
The body of a man was found in Saxon Woods Park in White Plains after he exited his stranded car and was swept away by flood waters.

The Mahwah River near Suffern rose above its minor flood stage of 5.0 feet at 10:30pm EDT. It then continued to rise, surpassing moderate flood stage (7.0 feet) and cresting at a height of 7.06 feet at 12:30am EDT on September 2nd. The river then gradually fell through the overnight hours, receding below minor flood stage by 10:45am EDT on September 2nd.
Flash flooding resulted in an estimated $60 million in damages across the Bronx, and an estimated $300 million city-wide. This estimate only includes FEMA and SBA fund requests.

Flash flooding resulted in an estimated $92.6 million in damages across Westchester County. This estimate includes $78 million in FEMA individual assistance to property owners, renters, and businesses and an additional $14.6 million in damages to Westchester County government infrastructure.
Some trees were blown down in Walnut Bayou community.
The Hutchinson River Parkway was closed in both directions in Pelham due to flooding between the Cross County Parkway and I-95.
All eastbound lanes of the Grand Central Parkway were closed due to flooding at the Van Wyck Expressway in Jamaica, Queens.
A tree was blown down.
At least 13 cars were submerged in flood waters on Cornelison Avenue in Jersey City.
Numerous trees down, one large tree down into a home.
The intersection of Cove Road and Seaside Avenue in Darien was closed due to flooding.
Doniphan closed due to flooding from Canutillo north to La Tuna to pump water.
Multiple basements were flooded in Eatons Neck.
Flooding was reported at the 28th Street subway station on 7th Avenue in Greenwich Village.
The basement of a home on Thorne Place in Rye was flooding.
Several cars were stranded in flood waters at the intersection of Bishop Avenue and Fenimore Road in Mamaroneck.

events.county: Long Island Sound W Of New Haven Ct To Port Jefferson Ny
events.narrative: A marine thunderstorm wind gust of 68 knots was measured at Eaton's Neck.
Photos shared on social media show deck collapse and several tree branches snapped. Time estimated by radar.
A 78 mph wind gust was measured at Eaton's Neck station at an elevation of 71 ft.
Tree down on Northern State Parkway westbound between Exit 27 N - Shelter Rock Road and Exit 26 N - New Hyde Park Road.
Water was entering a home in Jamaica, Queens.

events.county: Long Island Sound W Of New Haven Ct To Port Jefferson Ny
events.narrative: A marine thunderstorm wind gust of 42 knots was detected and estimated by Norwalk Light station.

The New York City Subway experienced flooding in many areas of the system and the MTA reported that service was extremely limited due to the flooding. This included reports of flooding at the Inwood-207th Street station (A line), excessive water on the tracks of the 2, 3, and 4 lines between Brooklyn and Manhattan, flooding of the N, R, and W lines in Manhattan and Queens, and major flooding at the 28th Street station on the 1, 2, and 3 lines in Chelsea. Service remained suspended on all but four lines at the start of the Thursday morning (September 2nd) rush. Overall the flooding resulted in an estimated $54 million in damage and repair costs to MTA infrastructure.
A large tree snapped in half on Countryside Drive.
Flash flooding was occurring on Holmes Road near the intersection with Greentree Road just to the east of NY-17.
Multiple cars were stranded in flood waters in Stamford with water rescues ongoing.

The wall of a basement apartment on 183rd Street near 90th Avenue in Jamaica, Queens collapsed due to flooding. A 43 year old woman and her 22 year old son were killed by the flood waters, while two others were rescued.
A 48 year old woman died when the basement of a home on Grand Central Parkway near the Horace Harding Expressway in Elmhurst flooded.
An 86 year old woman died when her basement apartment on 84th Street near 55th Road in Elmhurst, Queens flooded.
A 66 year old man died when his basement apartment on Ridgewood Avenue near Autumn Avenue in Cypress Hills, Brooklyn flooded.
The body of a man in his 40s was found floating in the Gowanus Canal near 25th Street and Third Avenue in Greenwood Heights, Brooklyn on Thursday, September 2nd.
An unidentified victim was found on the Grand Central Parkway near LaGuardia Airport inside a burned out car that had been rear ended. The fatality is believed to be flood related.
Flash flooding resulted in an estimated $60 million in damages across Queens, and an estimated $300 million city-wide. This estimate only includes FEMA and SBA fund requests.
Flash flooding resulted in an estimated $60 million in damages across Brooklyn, and an estimated $300 million city-wide. This estimate only includes FEMA and SBA fund requests.
Tree down on Meadowbrook State Parkway southbound at Exit M3 - Steward Avenue.
Water was gushing across Whittaker Road near the intersection with Levine Road.
A swiftwater rescue was needed for a man stuck on the roof of his submerged car on Big Woods Road near the Harris Road intersection and the confluence of Spring Brook and the East Mongaup river.
Heavy rain and flash flooding resulted in uninsured damages of $5,112,636 across Fairfield County.
A thunderstorm wind gust of 64 mph was measured at Jones Inlet-Point Lookout at height of 0 ft. AGL (3.5 FT. ASL).

The Hackensack River at New Milford rose above its minor flood stage of 6.0 feet at 11:15pm EDT. It then continued to quickly rise to moderate flood stage (8.0 feet) by 1:30am EDT September 2nd. The river ultimately rose above major flood stage (10.0 feet) at 5:00am EDT before cresting at a height of 11.03 feet at 9:15am EDT September 2nd. Thereafter the river gradually receded, falling below flood stage at 7:30am EDT September 3rd.||The crest of 11.03 feet is the third highest on record behind crests of 12.36 feet in April 2007 and 11.45 feet in September 1999.

events.county: South Shore Bays From Jones Inlet Through Shinnecock Bay
events.narrative: A marine thunderstorm wind gust of 34 knots was measured at Seaford-Ocean Avenue.
Grand Avenue in Park Ridge was impassable due to flooding at the Memorial Drive bridge. In addition, Grand Avenue at Kinderkamack Road and Pascack Road and Mill Road were also closed due to flooding.
The Northern State Parkway was closed westbound at Brush Hollow Road (Exit 34) in Westbury due to flooding.
Multiple cars were stranded in flood waters on I-95 near Bridgeport with water above the car doors.
Fairfield Police reported numerous flooded streets and road closures across town.
Water was 2-3 feet deep on roadways in Fresh Meadows, Queens. Several cars were submerged.

The Hackensack River at River Vale exceeded its minor flood stage of 5.5 feet at 11:30pm EDT. The river then continued to rise quickly, surpassing moderate flood stage (6.5 feet) by 12:15am EDT September 2nd and major flood stage (8.0 feet) by 12:30am EDT. The river then crested at a height of 11.05 feet at 4:00am EDT September 2nd. After falling through much of the morning, the river experienced a secondary crest of 10.73 feet at 3:45pm EDT September 2nd. The river did not fall back below flood stage until 11:45am EDT on September 3rd.||The crest of 11.05 feet is the third highest on record at this location behind crests of 12.26 feet in August 2011 and 12.19 feet in April 2007.

events.county: South Shore Bays From Jones Inlet Through Shinnecock Bay
events.narrative: A marine thunderstorm wind gust of 41 knots was measured at Captree at an elevation of 34 ft.
Significant flooding was reported in Park Slope, Brooklyn with at least 2-4 feet of flowing water on the road. Several cars were stranded.

events.county: Fire Island Inlet Ny To Moriches Inlet Ny From 20 To 40 Nm

Rolling Rock Road in Mountainside was impassable due to flooding.
Route 202 was closed near Pine Grove Court in Yorktown Heights due to heavy flooding.
Several roads in Winslow Township were closed due to flooding.

events.county: Long Island Sound East Of New Haven Ct/Port Jefferson Ny To The Mouth Of The Connecticut River
events.narrative: A marine thunderstorm wind gust of 34 knots was measured at New Haven Airport.

The Dirty Devil - Poison Springs Above Hanskville gauge indicated a rise from a baseline around 500 CFS to 14100 CFS, or from a gauge height of about 8 feet to about 21 feet. According to United States Geological Survey, the peak flow rate of 14100 CFS ranks as the 6th highest peak flow rate for all water years back to 1948. The peak gauge height of 21 feet ranks as the 3rd highest peak gauge height for all water years back to 1948.
TXDOT closed railroad frontage underpass because of flooding in Sierra Blanca.
The Fire Department reported several homes with basement flooding in Eatons Neck.
The West Haven Police closed Campbell Avenue in West Haven due to flooding.

events.county: Long Island Sound East Of The Mouth Of The Connecticut River
events.narrative: A marine thunderstorm wind gust of 46 knots was measured at Great Gull Island.
The entire ground floor of an apartment building in New Haven was flooded.
Significant flooding was reported into the first floors of multiple dorms at Yale University in New Haven.

Flash flooding resulted in an estimated $3,234,712 in damages across Suffolk County. This estimate is based on FEMA grant money awarded under the Individuals and Household Program (IHP), which includes funds for both housing assistance and other needs.
All lanes were closed due to flooding on the Major Deegan Expressway (I-87) northbound at Van Cortlandt Park South (Exit 11).
Thunderstorm wind gusts estimated at 60 to 70 MPH, tore two doors off of an outbuilding. Twelve inch diameter tree limbs were also reported down at this location.
Judson Avenue was reported impassable near Orton lane due to flooding.
The intersection at Cedar Lane and Marsh Road was reported closed due to flooding.
Road was reported closed due to flooding at the intersection of Route 63 and Hill House Road.
A road was reported closed due to flooding near the intersection of Route 126 and Route 63.
Route 317 in Woodbury was reported impassable due to flooding.
The water level rose above the flood stage of 10 feet, cresting at 10.62 feet at 6:00 AM EST on the 2nd of September. Wishard Road and Kemp Mill Road were both flooded.

The Port Jefferson Fire Department responded to numerous water rescue emergencies in the town. Multiple occupants were rescued by the department's high water unit, with some occupants found on the roof of their vehicles or trapped inside floating vehicles. There was also a landslide on Dark Hollow Road, which left the road impassable with 4 feet of debris. Eight families were evacuated from their apartment building on that road due to unstable conditions of the land.
Canal Street in Passaic was covered with several feet of water with water up to car roofs.
Flooding was reported on NY 440 southbound ramp to Arden Avenue in Fresh Kills. All lanes were closed.
The Bronx River Parkway was flooded southbound at East Gun Hill Road in Fordham. All lanes were blocked.

The Naugatuck River at Beacon Falls rose above its minor flood stage of 12.0 feet at 1:15am EDT, crested at a height of 12.79 feet at 2:00am EDT, and fell back below flood stage at 5:30am EDT. This is the 6th highest crest on record for the Naugatuck River at this location.

A NWS survey determined damage in Yarmouth to be from straight-line winds, with maximum gusts estimated around 80 mph.  The damage was concentrated in a small area along Old Hyannis Road, south of Corporation Road.  Numerous pine and oak trees were snapped and some were uprooted, generally all down to the north or northeast.

A weak tornado briefly touched down at 130 AM in Dennis early in the morning and lasted for less than one minute.  Damage was observed near the intersection of East Bay View Road and Wampanoag Trail.  One home sustained damage when a window of a sun porch was blown in and others on an adjacent side were blown out.  Outside patio furniture was lofted and landed across the street.  Another house across the street had shingles blown off the roof in the opposite direction from other damage that was observed.  Three large oak trees in the area also were blown down.  One resident received the tornado warning prior to 1 AM and was able to seek shelter in the basement.  The estimated maximum wind speed was 75 mph.
In Manchester, the Hop Brook overflowed its banks and inundated a large portion of Charter Oak Park.  In addition, farther north, portions of East Center Street (Route 44) were flooded.

events.county: Long Island Sound East Of The Mouth Of The Connecticut River
events.narrative: A marine thunderstorm wind gust of 42 knots was measured at the New London Coast Guard Academy station.
The Bourne rotary was flooded with two cars stuck in the water.  Basement flooding also occurred in the area.

In Worcester, numerous roads were closed due to flooding, especially on the west and south sides of the city.  At 155 AM EDT (1255 AM EST), Cambridge Street was flooded and impassable.  At 211 AM EDT, Merrick Street at Pelham Street was closed due to flooding.  At 230 AM EDT, parts of Southbridge Street and parts of Quinsigamond Avenue were closed due to flooding.  At 318 AM EDT, a car was stuck in flooded waters at the intersection of Cambridge Street and Kansas Street.

The water level along the Town Creek in Oldtown rose above flood stage of 14 feet, cresting at 15.11 feet on the 2nd of September at 2:30 AM EST. Water overflowed thee banks just downstream of the Pack Horse Road bridge.
In Southwick, the intersection of U.S. Route 202 and State Highway 168 was flooded and impassable.
In Dudley, West Main Street was flooded and impassable.

Heavy rain over the Little Colorado River Basin and tributaries created a surge of water at the river gauge (LCCA3) on the Little Colorado River near Cameron.  The water rose from 1.8 feet to 5.43 feet on the gauge in less than 15 minutes at 1245 AM on 2 September.  The water was still above 4.7 feet at 945 AM.
Multiple roads closed due to flooding around Thurmont.
Several streets were impassible in Meriden due to significant flash flooding.
In Ayer, Bishop Road was closed from Fort Devens to MacPherson Road due to flooding.
In Winchester, Cross Street and the Cross Street Bridge near the Aberjona River was closed due to flooding.

events.county: Long Island Sound East Of The Mouth Of The Connecticut River
events.narrative: A marine thunderstorm wind gust of 43 knots was measured at Great Gull Island at elevation of 53 ft.
In Webster, Route 12 (Worcester Road) at Tanner Road was flooded and impassable.  Other sections of Route 12 were flooded.
In Millbury, a car was stuck in flood waters on Grafton Street.

Highway 191 was closed due to flooding over the highway at Mile Post 491.8 between Round Rock and Rock Point (by Whale Rock) at 1135 PM. A social media video post showed a dangerous swollen wash along Highway 191.
Flooding was reported on the eastbound ramp from the center tube of the Lincoln Tunnel to 36th Street in Greenwich Village. All lanes were closed.
All lanes were closed due to flooding on the Saw Mill River Parkway northbound at the Ashford Avenue ramp in Ardsley.

In Fall River, flash flooding began as early as 247 AM EDT (147 AM EST), when Bedford Street and Stinziano Street became impassable.  The flash flooding then became widespread as rainfall increased. At 321 AM EDT, Cove Street was flooded and impassable.  A car was stuck in the flood waters and a person needed to be rescued.    By daybreak, numerous roadways were flooded and impassable.  Busy Route 24 was shut down in both directions due to flooding, with stalled vehicles blocking the highway.  The northbound ramp to Route 24 on I-195 also was flooded, with cars stuck.  A portion of Spencer Street had significant damage due to the rain.  On South Main Street, a building undergoing renovations collapsed due to the heavy rainfall.  A CoCoRAHS observer in Fall River recorded a total of 4.25 inches or rain but a CoCoRAHS observer in nearby Fairhaven recorded 6.34 inches.

events.county: Montauk Point To Moriches Inlet Ny Out 20Nm
events.narrative: A marine thunderstorm wind gust of 43 knots was measured at Napeague (3 W Hither Hills) station.

In Portsmouth, a large stretch of Fairview Lane was ripped up and destroyed due to flood waters rushing down the road and undermining the roadway.  CoCoRAHS observers reported a total of 8.32 inches of rain in Portsmouth and 7.56 inches in nearby Jamestown.
Several streets were closed due to flooding and several basements were flooded, but there were no evacuations needed in the city.
Multiple roads closed due to flooding in western Washington County.

In Middletown, Wood Road was flooded and impassable.  A basement of a home also was flooded.  A CoCoRAHS observer in Middletown recorded 6.42 inches of rain.  CoCoRAHS observers reported a total of 8.32 inches of rain in nearby Portsmouth and 7.56 inches in nearby Jamestown.

The Quinnipiac River at Wallingford rose above its minor flood stage of 10.0 feet at 3:15am EDT September 2nd. The river ultimately crested at a height of 11.25 feet at 6:15am EDT and 7:45am EDT before falling back below flood stage by 9:00am EDT.

In Boston, an underpass of Storrow Drive eastbound had flood waters 3-4 feet deep. A driver was trapped and was rescued.  On the MBTA line, train tracks on the Orange line were flooded in the vicinity of Ruggles, Back Bay, and Hyde Park.  In the Dorchester section of Boston, Morton Street at West Main Street was flooded and impassable.
A police vehicle was swept away by the swollen Weekeepeemee River at Jack's Bridge, resulting in the death of the Police Sergeant occupying the vehicle.
In Taunton, a car was stuck in flood waters on Washburn Street.
Heavy rain and flash flooding resulted in uninsured damages of $50,266 across Middlesex County.
A car was partially submerged in flood waters on Mill Street near State Street in Meriden. Mill Street was closed due to heavy flooding.
Flooding on Conococheague Creek.

The Yantic River at Yantic rose above its minor flood stage of 9.0 feet at 4:15am EDT. It then continued rising, climbing above moderate flood stage (9.5 feet) at 5:00am EDT, then above major flood stage (11.0 feet) at 6:30am EDT. The river crested at a height of 11.71 feet at 8:15am EDT. The river fell back below major flood stage at 11:00am EDT, below moderate flood stage at 4:15pm EDT, and finally below minor flood stage at 7:30pm EDT. The crest of 11.71 feet was the seventh highest on record for the Yantic River in this location.
In Brockton, a car was stuck in flood waters on North Main Street between Battles Street and East Main Street.  Report relayed by amateur radio operators.

Damage in Dartmouth was consistent with straight-line winds with maximum gusts estimated at 65 mph.  The damage occurred on Sunset lane and adjacent portions of Stoneledge Road to the north and Swift road to the south.  Large maple and oak trees were mostly blown down and some large branches were broken off of others.
In Peabody, Walnut Street was closed due to flooding.
Several roads were closed due to flooding in Waterford including Route 85 at the I-95 overpass, Gardiners Wood Road, and Old Colchester Road at I-395.
Heavy rain and flash flooding resulted in uninsured damages of $706,239 across New London County.

Power had to be turned off to numerous homes throughout Norwich for safety due to flooded basements. In addition, the Comfort Inn and Suites on Otrobando Avenue had to be evacuated due to more than 5 feet of water in the basement of the hotel. Three apartments in Mohegan Commons on East Baltic Street were flooded and uninhabitable.

The water level along the Licking Creek in Pectonville rose above flood stage, cresting at 11.19 feet at 10:15 AM EST on the 2nd of September. The access road to the river gauge off Pectonville Road was flooded, along with portions of Camp Harding Park, and low spots along Licking Creek Road.
In West Hartford, the Dept. of Public Works sent a Twitter photo showing that a large stretch of Fern Street, from Mountain Road to North Main Street, was closed due to flooding.

In East Hartford, Willow Brook went out of its banks, inundating parking lots and roadways at Rentschler Field at Pratt & Whitney Stadium.  Roads and buildings also were flooded elsewhere in town, including several homes.

In West Boylston, the Fire Department showed a Facebook photo of a driveway and part of a road was washed out by flood waters, with a white sedan hanging over the washed out road.  Exact street unknown.

In Bristol, the Copper Mine Brook overflowed its banks at the intersection of Mix Street and Farmington Avenue, flooding the busy intersection, nearby roadway, and some adjacent businesses and parking lots. Multiple additional roads were flooded.

In Bristol, boat rescues occurred at a small condominium complex on Main Street, along the Pequabuck River, which went out of its banks.  Multiple additional roads were flooded due to the Pequabuck River.
In South Windsor, the Podunk River overflowed its banks, flooding the first floor of the Mill on the River Restaurant.

In Vernon, for the second time in two months, swiftly flowing flood waters from the Hockanum River inundated a roadway connecting Hartford Turnpike (Route 30) to the Colonial Corners shopping plaza, a hotel, and a few other businesses.  Over 100 guests at the hotel were stranded, with local officials creating an off-road path onto I-84 to get stranded guests out.
In Wareham, on Shangri-La Blvd., flash flooding fractured and washed out a portion of the roadway.
In Westfield, the media showed a Twitter photo of the Powdermill Brook overflowing its banks and leading to flash flooding on Greenwood Street in Westfield.
In Andover, the Hop River overflowed its banks, causing flash flooding on Long Hill Road, Bunker Hill Road, and Parker Bridge Roads.

In Waltham, adjacent to Lexington Street, significant flooding occurred in a parking lot full of unoccupied school buses.  Eight school buses were unable to be moved due to flood waters reaching as high as the engine battery levels.  Broadcast media showed a Twitter photo of this event.
Thunderstorm wind gusts were estimated by the public. The winds combined with small hail to strip leaves off trees.
In Plainville, there was a media photo of flood waters nearly up to the bottom of a stop sign at a dumpster site on Norton Place.

events.county: Englewood To Tarpon Springs Fl Out 20Nm
events.narrative: WeatherFlow site XLID New Pass Shoal Light reported a 39 mph wind gust.

events.narrative: Broadcast media shared a picture of a waterspout via social media off the coast of Marco Island. The same waterspout was observed by a trained spotter near Goodland. The waterspout moved little.
The hail broke a skylight on a home.

events.county: Chokoloskee To Bonita Beach Fl Out 20Nm
events.narrative: A marine thunderstorm wind gust of 39 mph (34 kt) was measured by the CWOP Mesonet station FW8551 located in Marco Island.

Multiple reports of flooding via members of the public and Florida 511. Video reports via social media of water covering the right lane of NW 27 Avenue, just north of Flagler Street. Water extended past the curb and covered the adjacent sidewalk and a bus stop. Also, reports of flooding on SR 836 westbound blocking two right lanes. Rainfall observations from the general area indicated about 3 inches of rain.
Reports of flooding via social media of flooding near the intersection of Collins Avenue and 40th Street. Rainfall observations from the general area indicated about 1-3 inches of rain.

Multiple reports of flooding via members of the public and an off duty NWS meteorologist. Video reports were received via social media of street flooding in Downtown Miami and Brickell. Water was fairly deep in the right two lanes of Biscayne Boulevard southbound and water almost halfway up vehicle tires in a parking lot north of the Freedom Tower. Also, reports were received of standing water at knee level (around 1-2 feet deep) near Mary Brickell Village and adjacent locations, causing vehicles to stall and become stranded, as well as water encroaching on businesses.   Sandbags had to be used to keep water from entering.  ||Rainfall observations from the general area indicated about 3 inches of rain.
Blake Ranch Road was flooded with six inches of flowing water in four places.
Law Enforcement reported the gust.
The English Village Dugway automated weather station recorded a peak wind gust of 59 mph.

events.narrative: U.S. Space Force (USSF) wind tower 714, located near the Merritt Island National Wildlife Refuge, measured a wind gust of 45 knots from the southwest.
A wind gust of 58 mph from the west was recorded at the NASA Shuttle Landing Facility (KTTS).

events.county: Volusia-Brevard County Line To Sebastian Inlet 0-20Nm
events.narrative: The AWOS at the NASA Shuttle Landing Facility (KTTS) measured a wind gust of 50 knots from the west.

events.county: Hawk Channel From Ocean Reef To Craig Key Out To The Reef
events.narrative: A northwest wind gust of 38 knots was measured at an automated WeatherFlow station at Carysfort Reef Light.
Tree limbs 3 to 4 inches in diameter blown down, and dime to penny sized hail.

The water level along the Conowingo Dam rose above the flood stage of 23.5 feet, cresting at 24.29 feet at 8:00 PM EST on the 2nd of September. Minor flooding occurred in the town of Port Deposit Maryland.
